newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia health strike continues, could spread.
newsitem.headline: Colombia health strike continues, could spread.

text.p: A strike by doctors, nurses and other health workers continued across Colombia on Wednesday, a union leader said, amid signs that it could spread to other state sectors.
The stoppage, which started on Tuesday, was called in protest at government failure to honour a wage deal reached after a nationwide strike by state workers in February.

Leaders of the country's main labour federations, which represent about 800,000 workers in all state sectors, said late on Tuesday they would back the strike from June 11 if the demands of health workers were not resolved.

Union leaders said an estimated 120,000 health workers joined the strike, but Deputy Health Minister Juan Carlos Giraldo said many had shunned the strike call and only about one-third of state-run hospitals had been hit.
A union leader said emergency treatment, which continued despite the strike, made things appear semi-normal.

"The strike is continuing in state-run facilities...But a large part of the work of these centres is emergency treatment. These services are being maintained which gives an appearance of relative normality," Salvador Varela, a regional leader of the Medical Union (ASMEDAS), said.

ASMEDAS national leader Pedro Contreras said the strike had hit more than 640 hospitals and 6,500 health centres. Varela said the strike was beginning to spread to many of the 1,800 hospitals and health centres run by the decentralized social security system.

But Giraldo told reporters: "It's a strike where there's no unanimity. Many hospitals and health centres called on the goodwill of their workers, aware that this is an essential service and that strikes are harmful to the general population."
He said emergency services were not affected anywhere and patients waiting for routine treatment and operations could be referred to private clinics.

Doctors in Colombia's state-run hospitals earn about $900 a month and nurses between $300 and $550. Under the February wage deal, all state workers were to receive a wage hike of about 20 percent with extra payments to health workers to bring their salaries into line with other professions.
